E1: On scenario B, where treatment is randomised and the true effect is zero, the four estimators that assume randomisation or unconfoundedness reject a true null at close to the nominal 5% rate: difference_in_means 0.06, lin_regression 0.06, ipw 0.05 and aipw 0.06, each from 100 fits with a Monte Carlo standard error of about 0.02.
E2: On the randomised scenario A, difference_in_means covers the true effect 95% of the time (100 fits, standard error 0.022), which is the nominal level.
E3: On the confounded scenario D, difference_in_means is biased by 0.135 (standard error 0.003) and its interval covers the true effect only 6% of the time, while aipw is within 0.003 of the truth (standard error 0.004). Scenario G shows the same split: difference_in_means is biased by 0.167 and covers 2% of the time, while ipw, lin_regression and aipw stay within 0.014 of the truth and near 95% coverage.
E4: On scenario P4, staggered adoption with effects that differ across cohorts, twfe is biased by -1.06 (standard error 0.036), a sign reversal, and its interval covered the true effect in none of the 100 fits. callaway_santanna is within 0.006 of the truth (standard error 0.014), and hierarchical_did is within 0.019 with 92% coverage; event_study is biased by 0.67 and covers 3% of the time. Separately, callaway_santanna's coverage sits below the nominal level on P1 to P4 and P6, between 0.85 and 0.91 with a standard error of about 0.03, even where its bias is small; this is a gap of about two standard errors and is best read as suggestive.
E5: This expectation failed: hierarchical_did's pooled credible-interval coverage is 0.75 (standard error 0.019, 500 fits over P1 to P5), below the 0.90 threshold. The shortfall comes from one scenario. On P1 to P4 its coverage is 0.97, 0.93, 0.92 and 0.92, and its bias is within 0.07 of the truth. On P5, a scenario built to violate parallel trends, its coverage is 0.00 and its bias is 2.19. That is a shared pattern, not a weakness of this estimator alone: on P5 twfe is biased by 1.33, callaway_santanna by 1.78 and event_study by 2.28, and each of the three covered the true effect in none of its 100 fits. The expectation pooled a scenario designed to defeat the assumption every difference-in-differences estimator relies on, so a pooled figure near 0.90 was never available to it. hierarchical_did's own donor-pool rows, fitted for the first time in this study, are excluded from this figure entirely rather than folded in -- see the coverage table and the note on the donor-pool arm below.
E6: On scenario H, where outcomes are missing, no estimator produced a fitted result. The five estimators eligible for cross-sectional data each refused all 100 fits, and the remaining estimators are ineligible for cross-sectional data.
E7: hierarchical_did is the slowest estimator at a mean of 63.9 seconds per fit (standard error 1.9, 500 fits), ahead of aipw at 13.5 seconds and event_study at 9.9 seconds. This run's wall-clock figures were measured under heavier machine contention than the original study's (which measured 49.2 seconds for hierarchical_did), so the ranking still holds but the absolute seconds are not directly comparable across runs. Donor-pool rows are excluded from this ranking; bsts, hierarchical_did and synthetic_control are the only estimators fitted on the donor-pool arm.
E8: All 4,300 cells of the study are present with an intact stored result, and no unfinished results remain.
